'''丹生川上神社'''（にうかわかみじんじゃ）は、{{jalink|奈良県|Q131287}}{{jalink|吉野郡|Q1154558}}{{jalink|東吉野村|Q1203148}}にある{{jalink|神社|Q845945}}。{{jalink|式内社}}（{{jalink|名神大社|Q9610964}}）、{{jalink|二十二社|Q215320}}（下八社）の一社。{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|旧社格}}は{{jalink|近代社格制度#官社|Q712534|官幣大社}}で、現在は{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}の{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}。 === 社名について === 古くは「雨師明神」と称され、{{jalink|江戸時代|Q184963}}からは「蟻通明神」とも称された。 {{jalink|大正|Q329174}}以降、吉野郡{{jalink|川上村 (奈良県)|Q1204424|川上村}}の{{jalink|丹生川上神社上社|Q10877366}}・同{{jalink|下市町|Q1203064}}の{{jalink|丹生川上神社下社|Q10877367}}に対して「丹生川上神社中社」とも称されるようになったが、これは上下2社が既に存在したために、これを「中」としたもので、位置関係や社格の上下を表すものではない。 === 祭神 === 本殿と東殿・西殿の3殿に、以下の神々を祀る{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/about/|title=ご祭神／神社について|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 本殿：'''{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女神}}''' ** {{jalink|相殿|Q135009883}}に{{jalink|イザナギ|Q813858|伊邪奈岐命}}・{{jalink|イザナミ|Q682306|伊邪奈美命}} * 東殿：{{jalink|天照大神|Q455602|大日孁貴命}}・{{jalink|オモイカネ|Q586088|八意思兼命}}・{{jalink|応神天皇|Q317997|誉田別命}} * 西殿：{{jalink|開化天皇|Q333548}}・{{jalink|住吉三神|Q1114013|上筒男神}}・{{jalink|大国主|Q276944|大国主命}}・{{jalink|事代主|Q8009611|事代主命}}・{{jalink|ワタツミ|Q1474187|綿津見神}}・{{jalink|菅原道真公}} {{jalink|六国史|Q1151168}}では、「丹生川（河）上神」と地名を以て記され、具体的な神名を表すものはないが、古来朝野の{{jalink|雨乞い|Q477738|祈止雨祈願}}がしばしば行われ、雨を司る{{jalink|水神|Q3137449}}であったので、これを{{jalink|日本神話|Q814158|記紀神話}}に見える{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女神}}（みずはのめのかみ）や{{jalink|淤加美神|Q644201|龗神}}（おかみのかみ）に充てるようになった。また{{jalink|平安時代|Q193292}}初め頃から「雨師神」とも称されるようになったが初見は『{{jalink|日本後紀|Q1077029}}』{{jalink|大同 (日本)|Q1373191|大同}}3年（{{jalink|808年|Q30366}}）{{jalink|5月21日 (旧暦)|Q839620|5月壬寅（21日）}}条の「奉黒馬於丹生川上'''雨師神'''。以祈雨也」の記事。、{{jalink|雨師}}とは{{jalink|風伯}}と並ぶ古代中国の雨乞いの神なので、これは{{jalink|唐風文化}}への傾倒による神名であることは明らかである『{{jalink|抱朴子|Q831242}}』には「雨師者龍也」ともあり、{{jalink|竜蛇神}}でもある龗神との関連が指摘できる。。また、祈雨祈願の際には黒馬が、止雨の時には白馬（または青馬）が奉献される例であったが、これは{{jalink|馬}}を水神乃至はそれと密接な動物と見る観念に基づくものであり{{jalink|石田英一郎|Q6080158}}『{{jalink|河童駒引考}}』（1948年）参照。、また馬の色は、雨雲と黒、晴天と白という{{jalink|観念連合}}に基づく{{jalink|類感呪術|Q485000}}であろう{{jalink|ジェームズ・フレイザー|Q151936|フレイザー}}『{{jalink|金枝篇|Q651283}}』（1936年）参照。特に第1部第3章「共感呪術」及び第5章「天候の呪術的支配」には、祈雨の時に黒色の動物が、止雨祈願の時には白い（または赤い）動物が関係する事例を集めている。日本語訳では神成利男訳第1巻（国書刊行会、2004年）、または{{jalink|永橋卓介}}訳簡約版第1巻（岩波文庫、1951年）、吉川信訳初版上巻（ちくま学芸文庫、2003年）がある。。 現在の祭神は、{{jalink|大正|Q329174}}11年（{{jalink|1922年|Q2165}}）にそれまでの「大穴貴神・表筒男命・伊邪奈伎命」を変更したものである。 === 歴史 === 社伝に因れば、鎮座地は{{jalink|神武天皇|Q200188}}が{{jalink|神武東征#『日本書紀』|Q11590444|東征}}の際に、{{jalink|天津神||天神}}の教示により天神地祇を祀り、戦勝を占った地である『{{jalink|日本書紀|Q813935}}』神武天皇即位前紀戊午9月条に記載するが、これは{{jalink|宇陀市|Q863747}}榛原雨師鎮座の式内丹生神社の地であるとされている。。具体的には、神武は{{jalink|天香具山}}の土で作った平瓮と厳瓮を川に沈めさせ、椎根津彥に川魚の様子を観察させ、{{jalink|辰砂|Q104614|丹}}（水銀）の鉱脈があることを知り、500の真榊で諸神を祀り、国を平定することにした。 {{quote|而勅之曰「宜汝二人 到天香山 潛取其巓土 而可來旋矣。基業成否、當以汝爲占。努力愼歟。」… 時、椎根津彥、見而奏之。天皇大喜、乃拔取丹生川上之 五百箇 眞坂樹、以祭諸神。|日本書紀}} {{jalink|白鳳|Q11580612}}4年（{{jalink|675年|Q30523}}）に{{jalink|ミヅハノメ|Q8191796|罔象女神}}を御手濯（みたらし）川（{{jalink|高見川}}）南岸の現摂社丹生神社の地に奉斎し、その後現在地に遷座したものと伝えるが、{{jalink|寛平|Q1346292}}7年（{{jalink|895年|Q31119}}）の{{jalink|太政官符|Q11444013}}（『{{jalink|類聚三代格|Q11665185}}』所収）には、当時の丹生川上神社の{{jalink|祝 (神職)|Q24869239|祝}}や{{jalink|禰宜|Q11594490}}の{{jalink|解 (公文書)|Q11630902|解}}を引き、『名神本紀』という書に「『人声の聞こえない深山で我を祀れば、天下のために甘雨を降らし霖雨を止めよう』との神託により創祀した」との伝えがあることを記してる原文「丹生川上雨師神祝祢宜等解状称。謹検撿名神本紀云。不聞人声之深山吉野丹生川上。立我宮柱以敬祀者。為天下降甘雨止霖雨者。依神宣造件社」。ちなみにこの{{jalink|官符}}は近在の{{jalink|百姓|Q843939}}や{{jalink|浪人|Q212418}}がしばしば神地を穢すので、当時当社を「別社」として管掌していた大和神社神主の求めにより、当社境域の四至を定め、禁制を課すために下されたもので、その四至境域の記述は、論社考証に決定的な役割を果たした。。{{jalink|吉田兼倶|Q723266}}撰といわれる『{{jalink|二十二社注式}}』には、{{jalink|天武天皇|Q335181}}の白鳳乙亥年（4年）に{{jalink|垂迹}}し、{{jalink|大和神社|Q245731}}（{{jalink|天理市|Q502196}}鎮座）の別宮になったと記されているので、{{jalink|吉野|Q15410122}}と浅からぬ関係にあった同天皇によって創祀されたものとされている{{jalink|松田寿男}}『丹生の研究』、早稲田大学出版部、1974年。。古来大和神社の別社とされ古老の伝えに、大和神社の{{jalink|末社|Q135009906}}である「雨師明神」（現 高龗神社）を{{jalink|勧請}}したものという。、祈止雨の霊験著しい'''雨師神'''として、{{jalink|朝廷 (日本)|Q30253177|朝廷}}から重んじられ、763年より{{jalink|応仁の乱|Q385676}}の頃までに雨乞い、雨止めの奉幣祈願が96度されたと記録にみられ{{Cite web|和書|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=丹生川上神社のご由緒について|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=東吉野村観光協会}}、{{jalink|宝亀|Q18520676}}4年 （{{jalink|773年|Q31131}}）には{{jalink|神戸 (民戸)|Q11589711|神戸}}4烟が充てられている（『{{jalink|続日本紀|Q611399}}』）。{{jalink|律令制|Q742460}}時代を通じて{{jalink|祈雨神祭}}祭神に預かり、祈止雨祈願のために{{jalink|貴船神社|Q276779|貴布禰社}}とともに{{jalink|奉幣|Q11445508}}がなされた例は枚挙に遑がないが、その折には{{jalink|奉幣使}}に大和神社の神主が従う定めとされていた『延喜式』臨時祭祈雨神祭条。なお、『大倭神社注進状』には、この規定は大和神社の別宮であるためであると記している。。『{{jalink|延喜式神名帳|Q11064932}}』では{{jalink|社格#官社（式内社）|Q10444029|官幣大社}}（名神大社）に列格し、律令制の弛緩に際しても、{{jalink|二十二社|Q215320}}の1社にもなるなど朝廷からの厚い崇敬は変わらなかったが、次第に奉幣も減少するなど衰微していき、応仁の乱以降は、ついにその所在すら不明となるに至った。なお、社伝では中世以降たびたび造改築されたことが伝えられており、当神社所蔵の{{jalink|慶安|Q1146135}}3年（{{jalink|1650年|Q6951}}）の造営の上梁文には、当初の鎮座地に丹生神社を新造するとともに、本社を{{jalink|金剛峯寺|Q1203429}}の{{jalink|鎮守神|Q97479976}}に倣って「蟻通明神」と改称した旨が記されている。 近世以降『神名帳』の研究が盛んになり、特に式内社の所在地が問題とされるようになると、まず丹生川上神社下社が式内大社丹生川上神社に比定され、次いで{{jalink|明治|Q3125096}}に入って上社が比定されたが、{{jalink|1915年|Q2084}}（{{jalink|大正|Q329174}}4年）に{{jalink|森口奈良吉}}が『丹生川上神社考』を著し、明治以降{{jalink|近代社格制度|Q712534|郷社}}に列していた当神社が式内丹生川上神社であることを考証し、その後の調査でそれが立証されたため、同11年に社名を「蟻通神社」から「丹生川上神社」に改称、上下2社に対して「中社」を称するとともに、3社を合わせて「官幣大社丹生川上神社」として社務所が置かれるなど、当神社がその中心に位置づけられた。第二次大戦後の官制廃止にともなって、{{jalink|1952年|Q5272}}（{{jalink|昭和|Q327567}}27年）に3社はそれぞれ独立、当神社は現在{{jalink|神社本庁|Q908077}}に属して、その{{jalink|別表神社|Q10898274}}とされている。 === 神階 === {{jalink|弘仁|Q1373070}}9年（{{jalink|818年|Q25083}}）に従五位下が授けられ（『{{jalink|日本紀略|Q1053542}}』所引『続日本紀』）、その後{{jalink|承和 (日本)|Q1075605|承和}}7年（{{jalink|840年|Q29936}}）正五位下、同10年従四位下（以上『続日本紀』）、{{jalink|嘉祥|Q1373157}}3年（{{jalink|850年|Q30364}}）正四位下（『{{jalink|文徳天皇実録}}』）、{{jalink|貞観 (日本)|Q1075635|貞観}}元年（{{jalink|859年|Q23897}}）従三位、{{jalink|元慶|Q747451}}元年（{{jalink|877年|Q23905}}）正三位へと累進した（以上『{{jalink|日本三代実録|Q1052981}}』）。ちなみに、『{{jalink|大倭神社注進状}}』には、寛平9年（{{jalink|897年|Q30468}}）に従二位へ昇ったと記されている。 === 祀官 === 中世以来{{jalink|安土桃山時代|Q319531}}まで{{jalink|小川氏|Q135692551}}が神主職を襲い、また{{jalink|別当寺院}}として金剛峯寺{{jalink|末寺|Q11519671}}の'''摩尼山大乗院'''が奉仕してきた。小川氏は当地一帯（小川郷）の領主と宇陀郡雨師荘の{{jalink|荘官|Q11618914}}を兼帯し（従って同荘に鎮座する式内丹生神社をも所管した）、在地領主として勢力を誇った（{{jalink|南北朝時代 (日本)|Q264012|南北朝時代}}には{{jalink|北畠氏}}に属し、また{{jalink|長禄|Q1193524}}2年（{{jalink|1458年|Q6522}}）の神璽奪還（{{jalink|長禄の変|Q11653526}}）に活躍した{{jalink|小川弘光}}が著名である）が、{{jalink|天正|Q1145058}}6年（{{jalink|1578年|Q6707}}）に{{jalink|筒井順慶|Q8192220}}に屈してから衰退し、同15年（{{jalink|1587年|Q6744}}）に断絶した。以後、江戸時代を通じて大乗院が専管したが、これも明治5年に廃された。 === 境内 === * 拝殿 - 文政12年（1829年）より天保元年（1830年）にかけ建立。{{jalink|入母屋造|Q855025}}{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=拝殿／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 *東殿・西殿 - 文政11年（1828年）から約12年かけ建立される。両殿とも桧皮葺の流造{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_02|title=東殿・西殿／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。両殿ともに、一間社流造の3宇（殿）を相の間で接続し、一体の屋根をかけて5間社の1殿とした特殊な造り{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=丹生川上神社|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=東吉野村役場}}。 *本殿 - 文政11年（1828年）から約12年かけ建立される。桧皮葺の流造{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=本殿／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 :: 本殿は南面し、その左右に配祀神を祀る東殿・西殿が建つ。東西両殿はそれぞれ相の間で接続し、本殿から石段による渡殿が拝殿まで続く。 * 石灯籠 - 国指定重要文化財で、東殿前に立つ。高2.6メートルで竿に「丹生社 弘長二二年二九日 大工伊□□ 施主□右衛門尉」の刻銘がある（「二二年」は「四年」の意）川勝政太郎『日本石造美術辞典』（東京堂、1978）、p.197。刻銘の□は判読困難部分であるが、{{jalink|弘長|Q1327323}}4年（{{jalink|1264年|Q5514}}）{{jalink|伊行吉}}が造ったものとされる。伊行吉は名工・{{jalink|伊行末|Q21652391}}の息子。父・伊行末は、東大寺再興などの石工事を担い、伊行末の家系は伊派とも称され、鎌倉時代の名工の一門とされる{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=石灯籠（国指定重要文化財）／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 叶えの大杉 - 樹齢約1000年、樹高51.5メートル、幹廻り7.3メートルの大杉で、幹に両手を当て心願を口唱すればご利益がある{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=叶えの大杉／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * なでフクロウ - 叶え大杉に住み着いた「ふくろう」とされ、樹齢約200年の古木の山桜に彫刻した「なでふくろう」で、なでるとご利益がある{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=丹生のなでフクロウ／丹生川上神社|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 相生の杉 - 樹齢約800年の大杉で、2本が真直に立つ夫婦杉ともよばれている{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=相生の杉／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 真名井 - 本殿裏手の乎牟漏岳から本殿の地下を通る伏流水が井戸に湧いた御神水で、主祭神の罔象女神（水の神）のご利益がある{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=丹生の真名井(清めのお水)／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 茶室「甘雨」 - {{jalink|1969年|Q2485}}（昭和44年）竣工の社務所より渡り廊下で繋がる茶室{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=茶室『甘雨』／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 吉野離宮址 - 吉野離宮跡は発掘調査により宮滝遺跡（吉野町宮滝）であると、ほぼ確定しているが、丹生川上神社の神域地が吉野離宮跡との説がある。そのため1966年（昭和41年）10月に東吉野村郷土史蹟顕彰会にて「史蹟吉野離宮址」の顕彰碑が建立された{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=吉野離宮址（史跡）／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 爺婆石 （じじばばいし） - 西参道入口鳥居脇にあり、かつて吉野離宮の門柱とも伝わっていた。鳥居に向かって左側が爺石、右側が婆石で、夫婦石ともよばれている{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=爺婆石（じじばばいし）／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 神武天皇聖蹟碑 - {{jalink|1940年|Q18633}}（昭和15年）に文部省による第1回目の神武天皇聖蹟調査が実施され、神武天皇聖蹟「丹生川上の地」として当地が比定され{{Sfn|神武天皇聖蹟|1942|pp=165-173}}、本宮前（旧社地）象山（きさやま）の地に肇国由緒の地として碑を建立。聖蹟碑文には「神武天皇戊午年九月天下平定ノ為 平瓮及厳瓮ヲ造リ給ヒ丹生川上ニ 陟リテ天神地祇ヲ祭ラセラレ又丹 生川上ニ厳瓮ヲ沈メテ祈リ給ヘリ 聖蹟ハ此ノ地附近ナリ」と刻まれている{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_13|title=神武天皇聖蹟／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 夢淵 - 高見川、日裏川、四郷川の3つの川が合流し深い淵が作られている場所。古代、水神の鎮坐する霊境として、斎み潔めを行う場所として、斎淵（いみぶち）とよばれていたのが、「いめぶち」となり「ゆめぶち」とよばれるようになった。『日本書紀』によると、神武天皇大和平定のおりに、戦勝祈願のため丹生川上の地で厳瓮（御神酒を入れる瓶）を夢淵に沈め、酒に酔った大小の魚が流れることにより勝利を占った伝承地とされ、この時、水面に浮いて流れ出た魚が「魚」に「占」と書く「鮎」とされる{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=夢淵／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 東（ひむかし）の瀧 - 「秋津野の瀧」、「龍神の瀧」ともよばれる。日裏川が高見川に合流する場所にあり、龍神が棲むといわれ、吉野離宮の東にあるということから「東の瀧」とよばれるようになった{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_15|title=東の瀧／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 * 摂末社 ファイル:Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|叶えの大杉 ファイル:Manai（Sacred water） ofNiukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|真名井 ファイル:Jiji stone and Baba stone of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|西参道口の鳥居と爺婆石 ファイル:Niukawakami-jinja Yumebuchi(Tkami river) 001.jpg|夢淵辺りの高見川 ファイル:Higashi no Taki(East waterfall) of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|東の滝 === 摂末社 === === 摂社 === * 丹生神社 ** 祭神：弥都波能売命 :: 御手洗川（高見川）対岸の旧社地に鎮座するため「本宮」とも称される{{Cite web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_17|title=摂社・丹生神社／境内のご案内|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。本殿は{{jalink|春日造|Q3193781}}板葺。 :: 上述、{{jalink|慶安|Q1146135}}3年の上梁文によると、この時に鎮座したことになる。ちなみに、{{jalink|1915年|Q2084}}（大正4年）の「神社祭神変更並に社名変更許可書」に、当社の「御霊代ヲ本社ニ奉遷シ、丹生神社ニハ適当ノ御霊代ヲ奉安スルコト」とある。 ファイル:東吉野村小 丹生神社(丹生川上神社摂社) Niu-jinja, Omura 2011.2.22 - web|和書|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=祭典・年中行事|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=丹生川上神社}}。 *1月16日 - 末社水神社祭 *4月16日 - 末社木霊神社例祭 *4月17日 - 末社東照宮例祭 *6月4日 - 水神祭。水力発電・水道事業など水に携わる企業関係者などが参列する。 *7月16日 - 摂社丹生神社例祭。 *10月第2日曜日 - 小川まつり（太鼓台奉舁安全祈願祭）別名「喧嘩祭り」。以前は{{jalink|9月16日 (旧暦)|Q840252|旧暦9月16日}}に行われたが、大正11年に改めた。「壇尻（だんじり）祭」とも称し、氏子区内から8基の太鼓台が繰り出し、境内を乱舞する。大和三大祭りの一つである。 *10月16日 - 例祭。 === 文化財 === === 重要文化財（国指定） === * '''石灯籠''' - 指定年月日：{{jalink|1963年|Q2755}}（昭和38年）2月14日{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=石燈籠／国指定文化財等データベース|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=文化庁}}。 === 天然記念物（国指定） === * '''{{jalink|丹生川上中社のツルマンリョウ自生地|Q121038166}}''' - 指定年月日：{{jalink|1957年|Q5311}}（昭和32年）5月8日{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=丹生川上中社のツルマンリョウ自生地／国指定文化財等データベース|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=文化庁}}。本殿後背の小牟漏岳に群生する。{{jalink|常緑樹林|Q1024867}}の明るい林床に生育する{{jalink|ヤブコウジ科|Q161260}}で、常緑のほふく性低木。{{jalink|雌雄異株|Q148681}}。茎は、初め直生し、その後ほふくする。長いものは1.5メートルに達し、花は6 - 7月ごろに開き、果実は晩秋 - 冬に赤熱する。{{jalink|シイ|Q1065400}}や{{jalink|サカキ|Q775470}}などの常緑樹林中の半陰地の斜面に群生する。明るく肥沃な所では他の雑草に負け、暗い所では衰退していく。種子による稚苗はほとんど見られず、主にほふく茎によって繁殖している{{Cite web|和書|url=https://db.yamahaku.pref.yamaguchi.lg.jp/script/detail.php?no=229|title=ツルマンリョウ|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=山口県立山口博物館}}。 === 奈良県指定文化財 === * '''木造罔象女神坐像　男神坐像　女神坐像　童形神坐像''' 20躯 - 指定年月日：{{jalink|2018年|Q25291}}（平成30年）2月2日{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=奈良県指定文化財一覧|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=奈良県|page=13|format=PDF}}。1躯は像高54センチメートル、{{jalink|一木造}}の「罔象女神坐像」で、日本最古の和装姿のものとされる。他に唐衣の女神像2躯、男神像4躯が奉安され、いずれも{{jalink|日本美術史#平安時代|Q11508877|藤原時代}}後期の作とされる。 {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}}| Founding = (tradition) {{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) |Temples, etc. = {{jalink|Road of pilgrimage to sacred places of Buddhism and Buddhism|Q10444949}}No. 41 (Nara No. 28) |Main shrine = Sangensha {{jalink|Ryuzo|Q210684}}{{jalink|cypress bark roof|Q90373477}} |Regular festival = {{jalink|October 16th|Q2963}} |Map = Japan Nara }} '''Niu Kawakami Shrine'' (Niu Kawakami Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}. {{jalink|Shikinaisha}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), one of the {{jalink|22 shrines|Q215320}} (Shimohachisha). {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. === About the company name === In ancient times, it was called ``Amashi Myojin,'' and from {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} it was also called ``Aritori Myojin.'' After {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{jalink|Kawakami Village (Nara Prefecture)|Q1204424|Kawakami Village}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine|Q10877366}} {{jalink|Shimoichi Town|Q1203064}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Lower The shrine|Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine. === Enshrined God === The following gods are enshrined in the main shrine, east hall, and west hall. * Main shrine: '''{{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Elephant Goddess}}''' ** {{jalink|Aiden|Q135009883}} to {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Mikoto}} and {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanagi Mikoto}} * East Hall: {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|Dainichikataka no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Omoikane|Q586088|Eight Will Kanemikoto}}, {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Hondabetsu no Mikoto}} * West Hall: {{jalink|Emperor Kaika|Q333548}}, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|Kamitsutsu Ogami}}, {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Great Country Lord's life}}・{{jalink|Kotolord|Q8009611|Kotolord's life}}・{{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumigami}}・{{jalink|Michizane Sugawara}}In {{jalink|Rokukokushi|Q1151168}}, the place name is written as "Nyukawa (river) Kami-kami", and there is no specific name of the god, but since ancient times, Asano's {{jalink|rain prayer|Q477738|prayer to stop rain}} has often been held, and the {{jalink|water god|Q3137449} is said to be in charge of rain. }, so this money was used for {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Shozo Goddess}} (Mizuhanome no Kami) and {{jalink|Nakamikami|Q644201|龗God}} (Okami no Kami), which appear in {{jalink|Japanese Mythology|Q814158|Kikiki Mythology}}. Also, from the beginning of the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, it came to be called ``Amaishikami,'' but it was first seen in ``{{jalink|Japan Later Period|Q1077029}}'' {{jalink|Dado (Japan)|Q1373191|Dado}} 3rd year ({{jalink|808 years|Q30366}}) {{jalink|May 21 (Lunar Calendar) | Q839620 | May Jintora (21st)}} article "Hokurobao Nyu Kawakami''' Amashigami'''. Ikari Amaya". , {{jalink|Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{jalink|Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{jalink|Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that ``{{jalink|Hoboku|Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{jalink|dragon and snake god}}. . In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{jalink|horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.{{jalink|Eiichiro Ishida|Q6080158}} "{{jalink|Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). , and the color of the horse is probably {{jalink|similarity magic|Q485000}} based on the {{jalink|ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. Japanese translations include Volume 1 translated by Toshio Kaminari (Kokusho Kankokai, 2004), Volume 1 translated by {{jalink|Takusuke Nagahashi}} (Iwanami Bunko, 1951), and Volume 1 translated by Shin Yoshikawa (Chikuma Gakugei Bunko, 2003). .The current enshrined deities were changed in {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}11 ({{jalink|1922|Q2165}}) from the previous ``Oana Takakami, Omotesu Otoko-no-Mikoto, and Izanaki-no-Mikoto.'' === History === According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{jalink|Amatsukami||Tenjin}} during his {{jalink|Jinmu East Conquest#'Nihonshoki''|Q11590444|Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{jalink|Uda City|Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. . Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{jalink|Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{jalink|cinnabar|Q104614|tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country. {{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q81 91796|The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{jalink|Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. It is said that in {{jalink|Kanpei|Q1346292}}7 ({{jalink|895|Q31119}}) The mark |Q11444013}} (included in "{{jalink|Ruiju Sandaikaku|Q11665185}}") contains the (Priest)|Q24869239|Celebration}} and {{jalink|Negi|Q11594490}}'s {{jalink|solutions} (Official document)|Q11630902|Answer}}, the book ``Meishin Honki'' says, ``I was founded based on an oracle that said, ``If you enshrine me in a deep mountain where no human voice can be heard, I will rain sweet rain for the world and stop the rain.'''' Original text: ``Nyu Kawakami Amashi Shinto Blessing Negi Doto Interpretation Letter. Inspection of the Gods of God Honkiun. Fumonin's voice of Miyama Yoshino Nyu Kawakami. Tatega Shrine Pillar is worshiped. Tameten descends sweet rain stops the rain. Igami Senzozotensha''. By the way, this {{jalink|official sign}} was created at the time because the nearby {{jalink|peasants|Q843939}} and {{jalink|ronin|Q212418}} often polluted the sacred land. It was issued at the request of the priest of Yamato Shrine, who was in charge of the shrine as a ``Bessatsusha,'' to define the four limits of the shrine's boundaries and impose prohibitions, and the description of the four limits of the shrine played a decisive role in the historical analysis of the Ronsha. . {{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}}) is said to have been compiled by {{jalink|Kaneki Yoshida|Q723266}}. It is said that it became a annex shrine for the enshrinement of K|Tenri City|Q502196}}, so it is said to have been established by the same Emperor, who had a close relationship with {{jalink|Yoshino|Q15410122}}{{jalink|Hisao Matsuda}}, Research on Niu, Waseda University Press, 1974. . Since ancient times, it has been a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine.According to an old legend, it is said to have been derived from ``Amashi Myojin'' (currently Takanoki Shrine), which is {{jalink|terminal shrine|Q135009906}} of Yamato Shrine. , he was respected by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} as a ``rain god'' with remarkable miraculous powers for praying for rain, and records show that from 763 to the {{jalink|Onin War|Q385676}}, prayers for rain and offerings to stop the rain were performed 96 times.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=About the history of Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Tourism Association}}, {{jalink|Houki|Q18520676}}4 ({{jalink|773|Q31131}}) (Minto)|Q11589711|Kobe}}4 smoke is allocated (``{{jalink|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399}}''). Throughout the {{jalink|ritsuryo system|Q742460}} period, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}}, and together with {{jalink|Kibune Shrine|Q276779|Kifune Shrine}}, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}} to pray for the rain to stop. jalink|hohei|Q11445508}} There are too many examples to enumerate, but on such occasions, the priest of Yamato Shrine was supposed to follow the {{jalink|hohei envoy}} ``Engishiki'' special festival prayer rain god ritual article. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. . In "{{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{jalink|shrine rank #government shrine (shikinaisha)|Q10444029|Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}}3 ({{jalink|1650|Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{jalink|guardian deity|Q97479976}} of {{jalink|Kongōbuji|Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{jalink|Meiji|Q31250 96}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} ({{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}4), {{jalink|Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534|Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{jalink|1952|Q5272}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}27), and this shrine currently belongs to {{jalink|Shrine Honcho|Q908077}} and is designated as its {{jalink|Bepped Shrine|Q10898274}}. === God level === In {{jalink|Honin|Q1373070}}9 ({{jalink|818|Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{jalink|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jowa}} 7th year ({{jalink|840|Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{jalink|850 years|Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{jalink|Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jogan}} 1st year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{jalink|877|Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{jalink|Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{jalink|897|Q30468}}). === Priest === Since the Middle Ages until the {{jalink|Azuchi-Momoyama period|Q319531}}, {{jalink|Ogawa clan|Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{jalink|sub-temple|Q11519671}} served as the {{jalink|Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{jalink|shokan|Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{jalink|Nanbokucho period) (Japan)|Q264012|In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{jalink|Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{jalink|Changroku Incident|Q11653526}}) in {{jalink|Changroku|Q1193524}}2 ({{jalink|1458|Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{jalink|Junkei Tsutsui|Q8192220}} in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{jalink|1587|Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896. === Precincts === * Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. :: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall. * Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{jalink|Igyokichi}} in {{jalink|Hirocho|Q1327323}}4 ({{jalink|1264|Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{jalink|Igyosue|Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Tea room "Amanu" - {{jalink|1969|Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. * Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{jalink|1940|Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' The main shrine is {{jalink|Kasugazukuri|Q3193781}} thatched roof. :: According to the above-mentioned, {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}} 3rd year, it was enshrined at that time. By the way, in the {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} (Taisho 4) ``Permission to change the deity enshrined at shrines and change the company name,'' our company ``transferred the Goryodai to the head office and enshrined the appropriate Goryodai at Nyu Shrine.'' File: Higashiyoshino Village Elementary Niu-jinja (Nyu Kawakami Shrine Setsusha) Niu-jinja, Omura 2011.2.22 - panoramio.jpg|Nyu Shrine === Suesha === * Toshogu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|Tokugawa Ieyasu}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_16|title=Summer shrines, Toshogu Shrine and Mizu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. *Water Shrine - Deities enshrined: Takani no kami (enshrined deity at the upper shrine of Nyukawakami Shrine), Yami no kami (enshrined deity at the lower shrine of Nyu Kawakami Shrine). *Kodama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Goju no Mikoto}}. 1982 ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}57) To commemorate the 30th anniversary of the opening of the Ogawa-go Timber and Forest Products Cooperative Market, the shrine was founded at the request of {{jalink|Itaigeso Shrine|Q11379271}} (Wakayama City, Wakayama Prefecture){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_18|title=Suesha/Koda Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. File:Toshogu and Mizu-jinjya of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Toshogu Shrine is on the left of the two shrines on the stone steps, and Mizu Shrine is on the right. File:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Kodama Shrine Torii and Stone Steps to the ApproachFile:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 002.jpg|Kodama Shrine main building === Annual events === Main festivals {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=Festivals/Annual Events|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *January 16th - Suesha Mizu Shrine Festival *April 16th - Suesha Kirai Shrine Annual Festival *April 17th - Suesha Toshogu Shrine Festival *June 4th - Water God Festival. People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance. *July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival. *Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{jalink|September 16th (lunar calendar)|Q840252|September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato. *October 16th - Annual festival. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1963|Q2755}} (1963) February 14th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{jalink|Nyukawa Kaminakasha Shrine Natural Area|Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1957|Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{jalink|Evergreen forest|Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{jalink|Aperaceae|Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{jalink|evergreen forests|Q1024867}}. {{jalink|dioecious|Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{jalink|Chii|Q1065400}} and {{jalink|Sakaki|Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons. === Cultural property designated by Nara Prefecture === * '''Wooden Seated Statue of Elephant Goddess, Seated Statue of Male God, Seated Statue of Goddess, Seated Statue of Baby God''' 20 pieces - Designated date: {{jalink|2018|Q25291}} February 2, 2018{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}. One of the statues is a ``Seated Statue of the Elephant Goddess,'' which is 54 centimeters tall and made of {{jalink|one piece of wood}}, and is said to be the oldest statue in Japan dressed in Japanese clothing. In addition, two statues of goddesses in Chinese robes and four statues of male gods were enshrined, both of which are said to have been created in the late {{jalink|History of Japanese Art#Heian Period|Q11508877|Fujiwara Period}}. === Local information === ; Location * {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}Oaza and Small 968 ; Transportation access * From {{jalink|Haibara Station|Q5638969}} ({{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1531085|Kintetsu}}{{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1052545|Osaka Line}}, take the {{jalink|Nara Kotsu bus}} bound for Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba and get off at Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba. From Higashiyoshino Village Office, take the community bus bound for Shigo and get off at Aridori.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/life/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2020/03/hycommunitybus_guidan ce_r3.7.3.pdf|title=Community Bus [Furusato-go] User {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}}| Founding = (tradition) {{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) |Temples, etc. = {{jalink|Road of pilgrimage to sacred places of Buddhism and Buddhism|Q10444949}}No. 41 (Nara No. 28) |Main shrine = Sangensha {{jalink|Ryuzo|Q210684}}{{jalink|cypress bark roof|Q90373477}} |Regular festival = {{jalink|October 16th|Q2963}} |Map = Japan Nara }} '''Niu Kawakami Shrine'' (Niu Kawakami Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}. {{jalink|Shikinaisha}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), one of the {{jalink|22 shrines|Q215320}} (Shimohachisha). {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. === About the company name === In ancient times, it was called ``Amashi Myojin,'' and from {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} it was also called ``Aritori Myojin.'' After {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{jalink|Kawakami Village (Nara Prefecture)|Q1204424|Kawakami Village}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine|Q10877366}} {{jalink|Shimoichi Town|Q1203064}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Lower The shrine|Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine. === Enshrined God === The following gods are enshrined in the main shrine, east hall, and west hall. * Main shrine: '''{{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Elephant Goddess}}''' ** {{jalink|Aiden|Q135009883}} to {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Mikoto}} and {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanagi Mikoto}} * East Hall: {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|Dainichikataka no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Omoikane|Q586088|Eight Will Kanemikoto}}, {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Hondabetsu no Mikoto}} * West Hall: {{jalink|Emperor Kaika|Q333548}}, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|Kamitsutsu Ogami}}, {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Great Country Lord's life}}・{{jalink|Kotolord|Q8009611|Kotolord's life}}・{{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumigami}}・{{jalink|Michizane Sugawara}}In {{jalink|Rokukokushi|Q1151168}}, the place name is written as "Nyukawa (river) Kami-kami", and there is no specific name of the god, but since ancient times, Asano's {{jalink|rain prayer|Q477738|prayer to stop rain}} has often been held, and the {{jalink|water god|Q3137449} is said to be in charge of rain. }, so this money was used for {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Shozo Goddess}} (Mizuhanome no Kami) and {{jalink|Nakamikami|Q644201|龗God}} (Okami no Kami), which appear in {{jalink|Japanese Mythology|Q814158|Kikiki Mythology}}. Also, from the beginning of the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, it came to be called ``Amaishikami,'' but it was first seen in ``{{jalink|Japan Later Period|Q1077029}}'' {{jalink|Dado (Japan)|Q1373191|Dado}} 3rd year ({{jalink|808 years|Q30366}}) {{jalink|May 21 (Lunar Calendar) | Q839620 | May Jintora (21st)}} article "Hokurobao Nyu Kawakami''' Amashigami'''. Ikari Amaya". , {{jalink|Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{jalink|Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{jalink|Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that ``{{jalink|Hoboku|Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{jalink|dragon and snake god}}. . In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{jalink|horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.{{jalink|Eiichiro Ishida|Q6080158}} "{{jalink|Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). , and the color of the horse is probably {{jalink|similarity magic|Q485000}} based on the {{jalink|ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. Japanese translations include Volume 1 translated by Toshio Kaminari (Kokusho Kankokai, 2004), Volume 1 translated by {{jalink|Takusuke Nagahashi}} (Iwanami Bunko, 1951), and Volume 1 translated by Shin Yoshikawa (Chikuma Gakugei Bunko, 2003). .The current enshrined deities were changed in {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}11 ({{jalink|1922|Q2165}}) from the previous ``Oana Takakami, Omotesu Otoko-no-Mikoto, and Izanaki-no-Mikoto.'' === History === According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{jalink|Amatsukami||Tenjin}} during his {{jalink|Jinmu East Conquest#'Nihonshoki''|Q11590444|Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{jalink|Uda City|Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. . Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{jalink|Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{jalink|cinnabar|Q104614|tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country. {{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q81 91796|The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{jalink|Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. It is said that in {{jalink|Kanpei|Q1346292}}7 ({{jalink|895|Q31119}}) The mark |Q11444013}} (included in "{{jalink|Ruiju Sandaikaku|Q11665185}}") contains the (Priest)|Q24869239|Celebration}} and {{jalink|Negi|Q11594490}}'s {{jalink|solutions} (Official document)|Q11630902|Answer}}, the book ``Meishin Honki'' says, ``I was founded based on an oracle that said, ``If you enshrine me in a deep mountain where no human voice can be heard, I will rain sweet rain for the world and stop the rain.'''' Original text: ``Nyu Kawakami Amashi Shinto Blessing Negi Doto Interpretation Letter. Inspection of the Gods of God Honkiun. Fumonin's voice of Miyama Yoshino Nyu Kawakami. Tatega Shrine Pillar is worshiped. Tameten descends sweet rain stops the rain. Igami Senzozotensha''. By the way, this {{jalink|official sign}} was created at the time because the nearby {{jalink|peasants|Q843939}} and {{jalink|ronin|Q212418}} often polluted the sacred land. It was issued at the request of the priest of Yamato Shrine, who was in charge of the shrine as a ``Bessatsusha,'' to define the four limits of the shrine's boundaries and impose prohibitions, and the description of the four limits of the shrine played a decisive role in the historical analysis of the Ronsha. . {{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}}) is said to have been compiled by {{jalink|Kaneki Yoshida|Q723266}}. It is said that it became a annex shrine for the enshrinement of K|Tenri City|Q502196}}, so it is said to have been established by the same Emperor, who had a close relationship with {{jalink|Yoshino|Q15410122}}{{jalink|Hisao Matsuda}}, Research on Niu, Waseda University Press, 1974. . Since ancient times, it has been a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine.According to an old legend, it is said to have been derived from ``Amashi Myojin'' (currently Takanoki Shrine), which is {{jalink|terminal shrine|Q135009906}} of Yamato Shrine. , he was respected by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} as a ``rain god'' with remarkable miraculous powers for praying for rain, and records show that from 763 to the {{jalink|Onin War|Q385676}}, prayers for rain and offerings to stop the rain were performed 96 times.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=About the history of Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Tourism Association}}, {{jalink|Houki|Q18520676}}4 ({{jalink|773|Q31131}}) (Minto)|Q11589711|Kobe}}4 smoke is allocated (``{{jalink|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399}}''). Throughout the {{jalink|ritsuryo system|Q742460}} period, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}}, and together with {{jalink|Kibune Shrine|Q276779|Kifune Shrine}}, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}} to pray for the rain to stop. jalink|hohei|Q11445508}} There are too many examples to enumerate, but on such occasions, the priest of Yamato Shrine was supposed to follow the {{jalink|hohei envoy}} ``Engishiki'' special festival prayer rain god ritual article. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. . In "{{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{jalink|shrine rank #government shrine (shikinaisha)|Q10444029|Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}}3 ({{jalink|1650|Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{jalink|guardian deity|Q97479976}} of {{jalink|Kongōbuji|Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{jalink|Meiji|Q31250 96}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} ({{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}4), {{jalink|Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534|Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{jalink|1952|Q5272}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}27), and this shrine currently belongs to {{jalink|Shrine Honcho|Q908077}} and is designated as its {{jalink|Bepped Shrine|Q10898274}}. === God level === In {{jalink|Honin|Q1373070}}9 ({{jalink|818|Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{jalink|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jowa}} 7th year ({{jalink|840|Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{jalink|850 years|Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{jalink|Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jogan}} 1st year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{jalink|877|Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{jalink|Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{jalink|897|Q30468}}). === Priest === Since the Middle Ages until the {{jalink|Azuchi-Momoyama period|Q319531}}, {{jalink|Ogawa clan|Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{jalink|sub-temple|Q11519671}} served as the {{jalink|Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{jalink|shokan|Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{jalink|Nanbokucho period) (Japan)|Q264012|In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{jalink|Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{jalink|Changroku Incident|Q11653526}}) in {{jalink|Changroku|Q1193524}}2 ({{jalink|1458|Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{jalink|Junkei Tsutsui|Q8192220}} in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{jalink|1587|Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896. === Precincts === * Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. :: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall. * Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{jalink|Igyokichi}} in {{jalink|Hirocho|Q1327323}}4 ({{jalink|1264|Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{jalink|Igyosue|Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Tea room "Amanu" - {{jalink|1969|Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. * Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{jalink|1940|Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' It is located where the Hiragawa River joins the Takami River, and is said to be the home of the dragon god.As it is located east of the Yoshino Imperial Villa, it has come to be called the "East Falls"{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_15|title=East Waterfall/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Setsusha File:Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpgFile:Manai (Sacred water) ofNiukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Manai File:Jiji stone and Baba stone of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Torii and Baba stone at the west approach entrance File:Niukawakami-jinja Yumebuchi(Tkami river) 001.jpg|Takami River around Yumebuchi File:Higashi no Taki(East waterfall) of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|East waterfall === Setsusha === === Sessha === * Niu Shrine ** Enshrined deity: Yatsunami no Mikoto :: It is also called the "main shrine" because it is located on the former site of the shrine on the opposite bank of the Mitarai River (Takami River){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_17|title=Setssha/Nyu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. The main shrine is {{jalink|Kasugazukuri|Q3193781}} thatched roof. :: According to the above-mentioned, {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}} 3rd year, it was enshrined at that time. By the way, in the {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} (Taisho 4) ``Permission to change the deity enshrined at shrines and change the company name,'' our company ``transferred the Goryodai to the head office and enshrined the appropriate Goryodai at Nyu Shrine.'' File: Higashiyoshino Village Elementary Niu-jinja (Nyu Kawakami Shrine Setsusha) Niu-jinja, Omura 2011.2.22 - panoramio.jpg|Nyu Shrine === Suesha === * Toshogu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|Tokugawa Ieyasu}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_16|title=Summer shrines, Toshogu Shrine and Mizu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. *Water Shrine - Deities enshrined: Takani no kami (enshrined deity at the upper shrine of Nyukawakami Shrine), Yami no kami (enshrined deity at the lower shrine of Nyu Kawakami Shrine). *Kodama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Goju no Mikoto}}. 1982 ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}57) To commemorate the 30th anniversary of the opening of the Ogawa-go Timber and Forest Products Cooperative Market, the shrine was founded at the request of {{jalink|Itaigeso Shrine|Q11379271}} (Wakayama City, Wakayama Prefecture){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_18|title=Suesha/Koda Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. File:Toshogu and Mizu-jinjya of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Toshogu Shrine is on the left of the two shrines on the stone steps, and Mizu Shrine is on the right. File:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Kodama Shrine Torii and Stone Steps to the ApproachFile:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 002.jpg|Kodama Shrine main building === Annual events === Main festivals {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=Festivals/Annual Events|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *January 16th - Suesha Mizu Shrine Festival *April 16th - Suesha Kirai Shrine Annual Festival *April 17th - Suesha Toshogu Shrine Festival *June 4th - Water God Festival. People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance. *July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival. *Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{jalink|September 16th (lunar calendar)|Q840252|September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato. *October 16th - Annual festival. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1963|Q2755}} (1963) February 14th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{jalink|Nyukawa Kaminakasha Shrine Natural Area|Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1957|Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{jalink|Evergreen forest|Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{jalink|Aperaceae|Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{jalink|evergreen forests|Q1024867}}. {{jalink|dioecious|Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{jalink|Chii|Q1065400}} and {{jalink|Sakaki|Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons. === Cultural property designated by Nara Prefecture === * '''Wooden Seated Statue of Elephant Goddess, Seated Statue of Male God, Seated Statue of Goddess, Seated Statue of Baby God''' 20 pieces - Designated date: {{jalink|2018|Q25291}} February 2, 2018{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}. One of the statues is a ``Seated Statue of the Elephant Goddess,'' which is 54 centimeters tall and made of {{jalink|one piece of wood}}, and is said to be the oldest statue in Japan dressed in Japanese clothing. In addition, two statues of goddesses in Chinese robes and four statues of male gods were enshrined, both of which are said to have been created in the late {{jalink|History of Japanese Art#Heian Period|Q11508877|Fujiwara Period}}. === Local information === ; Location * {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}Oaza and Small 968 ; Transportation access * From {{jalink|Haibara Station|Q5638969}} ({{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1531085|Kintetsu}}{{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1052545|Osaka Line}}, take the {{jalink|Nara Kotsu bus}} bound for Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba and get off at Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba. From Higashiyoshino Village Office, take the community bus bound for Shigo and get off at Aridori.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/life/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2020/03/hycommunitybus_guidan ce_r3.7.3.pdf|title=Community Bus [Furusato-go] User Guide|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Office|date=2021.7.3|format=PDF}}. === Footnotes === {{Footnote help}} {{reflist|2}} === References === * "Shikiuchisha Research Report Volume 2 Yamato Province (A)" edited by Shikinaisha Research Association ({{jalink|Kogakkan University}} Publishing Department, 1982) * {{jalink|Naoichi Miyaji|Q11453535}} and {{jalink|Yuyoshi Saeki|Q11382847}} supervised "Great Dictionary of Shinto, reduced edition" ({{jalink|Rinkawa Shoten|Q11612454}}, 1969 ISBN 4-653-01347-0 (first edition {{jalink|Heibonsha|Q11482108}}, 1937)) * Edited by {{jalink|Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596}}, “Japanese Gods: Shrines and Sacred Places Volume 4 Yamato (New Reprint)” ({{jalink|Hakusuisha|Q4346470}}, 2000 ISBN 978-4-560-02504-8 (first edition 1985 ISBN 4-560-02214-3)) *{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1921034|title=Emperor Jimmu Sacred Site Survey Report|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=National Diet Library Digital Collection|year=1942|editor=Ministry of Education|pages=|ref={{SfnRef|Emperor Jimmu Sacred Site|1942}}}} === Related items === *{{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Kamisha|Q10877366}} *{{jalink|Nyukawakami
