{{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}}| Founding = (tradition) {{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) |Temples, etc. = {{jalink|Road of pilgrimage to sacred places of Buddhism and Buddhism|Q10444949}}No. 41 (Nara No. 28) |Main shrine = Sangensha {{jalink|Ryuzo|Q210684}}{{jalink|cypress bark roof|Q90373477}} |Regular festival = {{jalink|October 16th|Q2963}} |Map = Japan Nara }} '''Niu Kawakami Shrine'' (Niu Kawakami Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}. {{jalink|Shikinaisha}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), one of the {{jalink|22 shrines|Q215320}} (Shimohachisha). {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. === About the company name === In ancient times, it was called ``Amashi Myojin,'' and from {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} it was also called ``Aritori Myojin.'' After {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{jalink|Kawakami Village (Nara Prefecture)|Q1204424|Kawakami Village}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine|Q10877366}} {{jalink|Shimoichi Town|Q1203064}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Lower The shrine|Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine. === Enshrined God === The following gods are enshrined in the main shrine, east hall, and west hall. * Main shrine: '''{{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Elephant Goddess}}''' ** {{jalink|Aiden|Q135009883}} to {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Mikoto}} and {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanagi Mikoto}} * East Hall: {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|Dainichikataka no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Omoikane|Q586088|Eight Will Kanemikoto}}, {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Hondabetsu no Mikoto}} * West Hall: {{jalink|Emperor Kaika|Q333548}}, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|Kamitsutsu Ogami}}, {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Great Country Lord's life}}・{{jalink|Kotolord|Q8009611|Kotolord's life}}・{{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumigami}}・{{jalink|Michizane Sugawara}}In {{jalink|Rokukokushi|Q1151168}}, the place name is written as "Nyukawa (river) Kami-kami", and there is no specific name of the god, but since ancient times, Asano's {{jalink|rain prayer|Q477738|prayer to stop rain}} has often been held, and the {{jalink|water god|Q3137449} is said to be in charge of rain. }, so this money was used for {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Shozo Goddess}} (Mizuhanome no Kami) and {{jalink|Nakamikami|Q644201|龗God}} (Okami no Kami), which appear in {{jalink|Japanese Mythology|Q814158|Kikiki Mythology}}. Also, from the beginning of the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, it came to be called ``Amaishikami,'' but it was first seen in ``{{jalink|Japan Later Period|Q1077029}}'' {{jalink|Dado (Japan)|Q1373191|Dado}} 3rd year ({{jalink|808 years|Q30366}}) {{jalink|May 21 (Lunar Calendar) | Q839620 | May Jintora (21st)}} article "Hokurobao Nyu Kawakami''' Amashigami'''. Ikari Amaya". , {{jalink|Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{jalink|Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{jalink|Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that ``{{jalink|Hoboku|Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{jalink|dragon and snake god}}. . In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{jalink|horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.{{jalink|Eiichiro Ishida|Q6080158}} "{{jalink|Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). , and the color of the horse is probably {{jalink|similarity magic|Q485000}} based on the {{jalink|ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. Japanese translations include Volume 1 translated by Toshio Kaminari (Kokusho Kankokai, 2004), Volume 1 translated by {{jalink|Takusuke Nagahashi}} (Iwanami Bunko, 1951), and Volume 1 translated by Shin Yoshikawa (Chikuma Gakugei Bunko, 2003). .The current enshrined deities were changed in {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}11 ({{jalink|1922|Q2165}}) from the previous ``Oana Takakami, Omotesu Otoko-no-Mikoto, and Izanaki-no-Mikoto.'' === History === According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{jalink|Amatsukami||Tenjin}} during his {{jalink|Jinmu East Conquest#'Nihonshoki''|Q11590444|Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{jalink|Uda City|Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. . Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{jalink|Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{jalink|cinnabar|Q104614|tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country. {{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q81 91796|The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{jalink|Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. It is said that in {{jalink|Kanpei|Q1346292}}7 ({{jalink|895|Q31119}}) The mark |Q11444013}} (included in "{{jalink|Ruiju Sandaikaku|Q11665185}}") contains the (Priest)|Q24869239|Celebration}} and {{jalink|Negi|Q11594490}}'s {{jalink|solutions} (Official document)|Q11630902|Answer}}, the book ``Meishin Honki'' says, ``I was founded based on an oracle that said, ``If you enshrine me in a deep mountain where no human voice can be heard, I will rain sweet rain for the world and stop the rain.'''' Original text: ``Nyu Kawakami Amashi Shinto Blessing Negi Doto Interpretation Letter. Inspection of the Gods of God Honkiun. Fumonin's voice of Miyama Yoshino Nyu Kawakami. Tatega Shrine Pillar is worshiped. Tameten descends sweet rain stops the rain. Igami Senzozotensha''. By the way, this {{jalink|official sign}} was created at the time because the nearby {{jalink|peasants|Q843939}} and {{jalink|ronin|Q212418}} often polluted the sacred land. It was issued at the request of the priest of Yamato Shrine, who was in charge of the shrine as a ``Bessatsusha,'' to define the four limits of the shrine's boundaries and impose prohibitions, and the description of the four limits of the shrine played a decisive role in the historical analysis of the Ronsha. . {{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}}) is said to have been compiled by {{jalink|Kaneki Yoshida|Q723266}}. It is said that it became a annex shrine for the enshrinement of K|Tenri City|Q502196}}, so it is said to have been established by the same Emperor, who had a close relationship with {{jalink|Yoshino|Q15410122}}{{jalink|Hisao Matsuda}}, Research on Niu, Waseda University Press, 1974. . Since ancient times, it has been a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine.According to an old legend, it is said to have been derived from ``Amashi Myojin'' (currently Takanoki Shrine), which is {{jalink|terminal shrine|Q135009906}} of Yamato Shrine. , he was respected by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} as a ``rain god'' with remarkable miraculous powers for praying for rain, and records show that from 763 to the {{jalink|Onin War|Q385676}}, prayers for rain and offerings to stop the rain were performed 96 times.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=About the history of Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Tourism Association}}, {{jalink|Houki|Q18520676}}4 ({{jalink|773|Q31131}}) (Minto)|Q11589711|Kobe}}4 smoke is allocated (``{{jalink|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399}}''). Throughout the {{jalink|ritsuryo system|Q742460}} period, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}}, and together with {{jalink|Kibune Shrine|Q276779|Kifune Shrine}}, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}} to pray for the rain to stop. jalink|hohei|Q11445508}} There are too many examples to enumerate, but on such occasions, the priest of Yamato Shrine was supposed to follow the {{jalink|hohei envoy}} ``Engishiki'' special festival prayer rain god ritual article. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. . In "{{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{jalink|shrine rank #government shrine (shikinaisha)|Q10444029|Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}}3 ({{jalink|1650|Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{jalink|guardian deity|Q97479976}} of {{jalink|Kongōbuji|Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{jalink|Meiji|Q31250 96}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} ({{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}4), {{jalink|Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534|Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{jalink|1952|Q5272}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}27), and this shrine currently belongs to {{jalink|Shrine Honcho|Q908077}} and is designated as its {{jalink|Bepped Shrine|Q10898274}}. === God level === In {{jalink|Honin|Q1373070}}9 ({{jalink|818|Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{jalink|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jowa}} 7th year ({{jalink|840|Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{jalink|850 years|Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{jalink|Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jogan}} 1st year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{jalink|877|Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{jalink|Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{jalink|897|Q30468}}). === Priest === Since the Middle Ages until the {{jalink|Azuchi-Momoyama period|Q319531}}, {{jalink|Ogawa clan|Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{jalink|sub-temple|Q11519671}} served as the {{jalink|Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{jalink|shokan|Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{jalink|Nanbokucho period) (Japan)|Q264012|In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{jalink|Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{jalink|Changroku Incident|Q11653526}}) in {{jalink|Changroku|Q1193524}}2 ({{jalink|1458|Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{jalink|Junkei Tsutsui|Q8192220}} in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{jalink|1587|Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896. === Precincts === * Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. :: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall. * Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{jalink|Igyokichi}} in {{jalink|Hirocho|Q1327323}}4 ({{jalink|1264|Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{jalink|Igyosue|Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Tea room "Amanu" - {{jalink|1969|Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. * Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{jalink|1940|Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' It is located where the Hiragawa River joins the Takami River, and is said to be the home of the dragon god.As it is located east of the Yoshino Imperial Villa, it has come to be called the "East Falls"{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_15|title=East Waterfall/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Setsusha File:Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpgFile:Manai (Sacred water) ofNiukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Manai File:Jiji stone and Baba stone of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Torii and Baba stone at the west approach entrance File:Niukawakami-jinja Yumebuchi(Tkami river) 001.jpg|Takami River around Yumebuchi File:Higashi no Taki(East waterfall) of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|East waterfall === Setsusha === === Sessha === * Niu Shrine ** Enshrined deity: Yatsunami no Mikoto :: It is also called the "main shrine" because it is located on the former site of the shrine on the opposite bank of the Mitarai River (Takami River){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_17|title=Setssha/Nyu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. The main shrine is {{jalink|Kasugazukuri|Q3193781}} thatched roof. :: According to the above-mentioned, {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}} 3rd year, it was enshrined at that time. By the way, in the {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} (Taisho 4) ``Permission to change the deity enshrined at shrines and change the company name,'' our company ``transferred the Goryodai to the head office and enshrined the appropriate Goryodai at Nyu Shrine.'' File: Higashiyoshino Village Elementary Niu-jinja (Nyu Kawakami Shrine Setsusha) Niu-jinja, Omura 2011.2.22 - panoramio.jpg|Nyu Shrine === Suesha === * Toshogu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|Tokugawa Ieyasu}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_16|title=Summer shrines, Toshogu Shrine and Mizu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. *Water Shrine - Deities enshrined: Takani no kami (enshrined deity at the upper shrine of Nyukawakami Shrine), Yami no kami (enshrined deity at the lower shrine of Nyu Kawakami Shrine). *Kodama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Goju no Mikoto}}. 1982 ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}57) To commemorate the 30th anniversary of the opening of the Ogawa-go Timber and Forest Products Cooperative Market, the shrine was founded at the request of {{jalink|Itaigeso Shrine|Q11379271}} (Wakayama City, Wakayama Prefecture){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_18|title=Suesha/Koda Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. File:Toshogu and Mizu-jinjya of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Toshogu Shrine is on the left of the two shrines on the stone steps, and Mizu Shrine is on the right. File:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Kodama Shrine Torii and Stone Steps to the ApproachFile:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 002.jpg|Kodama Shrine main building === Annual events === Main festivals {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=Festivals/Annual Events|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *January 16th - Suesha Mizu Shrine Festival *April 16th - Suesha Kirai Shrine Annual Festival *April 17th - Suesha Toshogu Shrine Festival *June 4th - Water God Festival. People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance. *July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival. *Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{jalink|September 16th (lunar calendar)|Q840252|September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato. *October 16th - Annual festival. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1963|Q2755}} (1963) February 14th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{jalink|Nyukawa Kaminakasha Shrine Natural Area|Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1957|Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{jalink|Evergreen forest|Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{jalink|Aperaceae|Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{jalink|evergreen forests|Q1024867}}. {{jalink|dioecious|Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{jalink|Chii|Q1065400}} and {{jalink|Sakaki|Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons. === Cultural property designated by Nara Prefecture === * '''Wooden Seated Statue of Elephant Goddess, Seated Statue of Male God, Seated Statue of Goddess, Seated Statue of Baby God''' 20 pieces - Designated date: {{jalink|2018|Q25291}} February 2, 2018{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}. One of the statues is a ``Seated Statue of the Elephant Goddess,'' which is 54 centimeters tall and made of {{jalink|one piece of wood}}, and is said to be the oldest statue in Japan dressed in Japanese clothing. In addition, two statues of goddesses in Chinese robes and four statues of male gods were enshrined, both of which are said to have been created in the late {{jalink|History of Japanese Art#Heian Period|Q11508877|Fujiwara Period}}. === Local information === ; Location * {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}Oaza and Small 968 ; Transportation access * From {{jalink|Haibara Station|Q5638969}} ({{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1531085|Kintetsu}}{{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1052545|Osaka Line}}, take the {{jalink|Nara Kotsu bus}} bound for Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba and get off at Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba. After {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{jalink|Kawakami Village (Nara Prefecture)|Q1204424|Kawakami Village}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine|Q10877366}} {{jalink|Shimoichi Town|Q1203064}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Lower The shrine|Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine. === Enshrined God === The following gods are enshrined in the main shrine, east hall, and west hall. * Main shrine: '''{{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Elephant Goddess}}''' ** {{jalink|Aiden|Q135009883}} to {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Mikoto}} and {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanagi Mikoto}} * East Hall: {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|Dainichikataka no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Omoikane|Q586088|Eight Will Kanemikoto}}, {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Hondabetsu no Mikoto}} * West Hall: {{jalink|Emperor Kaika|Q333548}}, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|Kamitsutsu Ogami}}, {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Great Country Lord's life}}・{{jalink|Kotolord|Q8009611|Kotolord's life}}・{{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumigami}}・{{jalink|Michizane Sugawara}}In {{jalink|Rokukokushi|Q1151168}}, the place name is written as "Nyukawa (river) Kami-kami", and there is no specific name of the god, but since ancient times, Asano's {{jalink|rain prayer|Q477738|prayer to stop rain}} has often been held, and the {{jalink|water god|Q3137449} is said to be in charge of rain. }, so this money was used for {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Shozo Goddess}} (Mizuhanome no Kami) and {{jalink|Nakamikami|Q644201|龗God}} (Okami no Kami), which appear in {{jalink|Japanese Mythology|Q814158|Kikiki Mythology}}. Ikari Amaya". , {{jalink|Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{jalink|Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{jalink|Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that ``{{jalink|Hoboku|Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{jalink|dragon and snake god}}. . In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{jalink|horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.{{jalink|Eiichiro Ishida|Q6080158}} "{{jalink|Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). , and the color of the horse is probably {{jalink|similarity magic|Q485000}} based on the {{jalink|ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. Japanese translations include Volume 1 translated by Toshio Kaminari (Kokusho Kankokai, 2004), Volume 1 translated by {{jalink|Takusuke Nagahashi}} (Iwanami Bunko, 1951), and Volume 1 translated by Shin Yoshikawa (Chikuma Gakugei Bunko, 2003). .The current enshrined deities were changed in {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}11 ({{jalink|1922|Q2165}}) from the previous ``Oana Takakami, Omotesu Otoko-no-Mikoto, and Izanaki-no-Mikoto.'' === History === According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{jalink|Amatsukami||Tenjin}} during his {{jalink|Jinmu East Conquest#'Nihonshoki''|Q11590444|Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{jalink|Uda City|Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. . Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{jalink|Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{jalink|cinnabar|Q104614|tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country. {{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q81 91796|The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{jalink|Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. It is said that in {{jalink|Kanpei|Q1346292}}7 ({{jalink|895|Q31119}}) The mark |Q11444013}} (included in "{{jalink|Ruiju Sandaikaku|Q11665185}}") contains the (Priest)|Q24869239|Celebration}} and {{jalink|Negi|Q11594490}}'s {{jalink|solutions} (Official document)|Q11630902|Answer}}, the book ``Meishin Honki'' says, ``I was founded based on an oracle that said, ``If you enshrine me in a deep mountain where no human voice can be heard, I will rain sweet rain for the world and stop the rain.'''' Original text: ``Nyu Kawakami Amashi Shinto Blessing Negi Doto Interpretation Letter. Inspection of the Gods of God Honkiun. Fumonin's voice of Miyama Yoshino Nyu Kawakami. Tatega Shrine Pillar is worshiped. Tameten descends sweet rain stops the rain. Igami Senzozotensha''. By the way, this {{jalink|official sign}} was created at the time because the nearby {{jalink|peasants|Q843939}} and {{jalink|ronin|Q212418}} often polluted the sacred land. It was issued at the request of the priest of Yamato Shrine, who was in charge of the shrine as a ``Bessatsusha,'' to define the four limits of the shrine's boundaries and impose prohibitions, and the description of the four limits of the shrine played a decisive role in the historical analysis of the Ronsha. . {{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}}) is said to have been compiled by {{jalink|Kaneki Yoshida|Q723266}}. It is said that it became a annex shrine for the enshrinement of K|Tenri City|Q502196}}, so it is said to have been established by the same Emperor, who had a close relationship with {{jalink|Yoshino|Q15410122}}{{jalink|Hisao Matsuda}}, Research on Niu, Waseda University Press, 1974. . Since ancient times, it has been a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine.According to an old legend, it is said to have been derived from ``Amashi Myojin'' (currently Takanoki Shrine), which is {{jalink|terminal shrine|Q135009906}} of Yamato Shrine. , he was respected by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} as a ``rain god'' with remarkable miraculous powers for praying for rain, and records show that from 763 to the {{jalink|Onin War|Q385676}}, prayers for rain and offerings to stop the rain were performed 96 times.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=About the history of Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Tourism Association}}, {{jalink|Houki|Q18520676}}4 ({{jalink|773|Q31131}}) (Minto)|Q11589711|Kobe}}4 smoke is allocated (``{{jalink|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399}}''). Throughout the {{jalink|ritsuryo system|Q742460}} period, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}}, and together with {{jalink|Kibune Shrine|Q276779|Kifune Shrine}}, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}} to pray for the rain to stop. jalink|hohei|Q11445508}} There are too many examples to enumerate, but on such occasions, the priest of Yamato Shrine was supposed to follow the {{jalink|hohei envoy}} ``Engishiki'' special festival prayer rain god ritual article. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. . In "{{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{jalink|shrine rank #government shrine (shikinaisha)|Q10444029|Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}}3 ({{jalink|1650|Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{jalink|guardian deity|Q97479976}} of {{jalink|Kongōbuji|Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{jalink|Meiji|Q31250 96}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} ({{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}4), {{jalink|Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534|Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{jalink|1952|Q5272}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}27), and this shrine currently belongs to {{jalink|Shrine Honcho|Q908077}} and is designated as its {{jalink|Bepped Shrine|Q10898274}}. === God level === In {{jalink|Honin|Q1373070}}9 ({{jalink|818|Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{jalink|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jowa}} 7th year ({{jalink|840|Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{jalink|850 years|Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{jalink|Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jogan}} 1st year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{jalink|877|Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{jalink|Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{jalink|897|Q30468}}). === Priest === Since the Middle Ages until the {{jalink|Azuchi-Momoyama period|Q319531}}, {{jalink|Ogawa clan|Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{jalink|sub-temple|Q11519671}} served as the {{jalink|Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{jalink|shokan|Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{jalink|Nanbokucho period) (Japan)|Q264012|In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{jalink|Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{jalink|Changroku Incident|Q11653526}}) in {{jalink|Changroku|Q1193524}}2 ({{jalink|1458|Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{jalink|Junkei Tsutsui|Q8192220}} in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{jalink|1587|Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896. === Precincts === * Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. :: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall. * Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{jalink|Igyokichi}} in {{jalink|Hirocho|Q1327323}}4 ({{jalink|1264|Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{jalink|Igyosue|Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Tea room "Amanu" - {{jalink|1969|Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. * Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{jalink|1940|Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance. *July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival. *Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{jalink|September 16th (lunar calendar)|Q840252|September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato. *October 16th - Annual festival. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1963|Q2755}} (1963) February 14th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{jalink|Nyukawa Kaminakasha Shrine Natural Area|Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1957|Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{jalink|Evergreen forest|Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{jalink|Aperaceae|Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{jalink|evergreen forests|Q1024867}}. {{jalink|dioecious|Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{jalink|Chii|Q1065400}} and {{jalink|Sakaki|Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons. === Cultural property designated by Nara Prefecture === * '''Wooden Seated Statue of Elephant Goddess, Seated Statue of Male God, Seated Statue of Goddess, Seated Statue of Baby God''' 20 pieces - Designated date: {{jalink|2018|Q25291}} February 2, 2018{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}. One of the statues is a ``Seated Statue of the Elephant Goddess,'' which is 54 centimeters tall and made of {{jalink|one piece of wood}}, and is said to be the oldest statue in Japan dressed in Japanese clothing. In addition, two statues of goddesses in Chinese robes and four statues of male gods were enshrined, both of which are said to have been created in the late {{jalink|History of Japanese Art#Heian Period|Q11508877|Fujiwara Period}}. === Local information === ; Location * {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}Oaza and Small 968 ; Transportation access * From {{jalink|Haibara Station|Q5638969}} ({{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1531085|Kintetsu}}{{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1052545|Osaka Line}}, take the {{jalink|Nara Kotsu bus}} bound for Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba and get off at Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba. {{jalink|Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274}}| Founding = (tradition) {{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) |Temples, etc. = {{jalink|Road of pilgrimage to sacred places of Buddhism and Buddhism|Q10444949}}No. 41 (Nara No. 28) |Main shrine = Sangensha {{jalink|Ryuzo|Q210684}}{{jalink|cypress bark roof|Q90373477}} |Regular festival = {{jalink|October 16th|Q2963}} |Map = Japan Nara }} '''Niu Kawakami Shrine'' (Niu Kawakami Shrine) is located in {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}. {{jalink|Shikinaisha}} ({{jalink|Meishin Taisha|Q9610964}}), one of the {{jalink|22 shrines|Q215320}} (Shimohachisha). {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534|Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System#Government Shrine|Q712534|Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{jalink|Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274}} of {{jalink|Shrine Head Office|Q908077}}. === About the company name === In ancient times, it was called ``Amashi Myojin,'' and from {{jalink|Edo period|Q184963}} it was also called ``Aritori Myojin.'' After {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{jalink|Kawakami Village (Nara Prefecture)|Q1204424|Kawakami Village}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine|Q10877366}} {{jalink|Shimoichi Town|Q1203064}} {{jalink|Nyukawakami Shrine Lower The shrine|Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine. === Enshrined God === The following gods are enshrined in the main shrine, east hall, and west hall. * Main shrine: '''{{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Elephant Goddess}}''' ** {{jalink|Aiden|Q135009883}} to {{jalink|Izanagi|Q813858|Izanagi Mikoto}} and {{jalink|Izanami|Q682306|Izanagi Mikoto}} * East Hall: {{jalink|Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|Dainichikataka no Mikoto}}, {{jalink|Omoikane|Q586088|Eight Will Kanemikoto}}, {{jalink|Emperor Ojin|Q317997|Hondabetsu no Mikoto}} * West Hall: {{jalink|Emperor Kaika|Q333548}}, {{jalink|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|Q1114013|Kamitsutsu Ogami}}, {{jalink|Okuninushi|Q276944|Great Country Lord's life}}・{{jalink|Kotolord|Q8009611|Kotolord's life}}・{{jalink|Watatsumi|Q1474187|Watatsumigami}}・{{jalink|Michizane Sugawara}}In {{jalink|Rokukokushi|Q1151168}}, the place name is written as "Nyukawa (river) Kami-kami", and there is no specific name of the god, but since ancient times, Asano's {{jalink|rain prayer|Q477738|prayer to stop rain}} has often been held, and the {{jalink|water god|Q3137449} is said to be in charge of rain. }, so this money was used for {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q8191796|Shozo Goddess}} (Mizuhanome no Kami) and {{jalink|Nakamikami|Q644201|龗God}} (Okami no Kami), which appear in {{jalink|Japanese Mythology|Q814158|Kikiki Mythology}}. Also, from the beginning of the {{jalink|Heian period|Q193292}}, it came to be called ``Amaishikami,'' but it was first seen in ``{{jalink|Japan Later Period|Q1077029}}'' {{jalink|Dado (Japan)|Q1373191|Dado}} 3rd year ({{jalink|808 years|Q30366}}) {{jalink|May 21 (Lunar Calendar) | Q839620 | May Jintora (21st)}} article "Hokurobao Nyu Kawakami''' Amashigami'''. Ikari Amaya". , {{jalink|Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{jalink|Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{jalink|Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that ``{{jalink|Hoboku|Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{jalink|dragon and snake god}}. . In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{jalink|horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.{{jalink|Eiichiro Ishida|Q6080158}} "{{jalink|Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). , and the color of the horse is probably {{jalink|similarity magic|Q485000}} based on the {{jalink|ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. Japanese translations include Volume 1 translated by Toshio Kaminari (Kokusho Kankokai, 2004), Volume 1 translated by {{jalink|Takusuke Nagahashi}} (Iwanami Bunko, 1951), and Volume 1 translated by Shin Yoshikawa (Chikuma Gakugei Bunko, 2003). .The current enshrined deities were changed in {{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}11 ({{jalink|1922|Q2165}}) from the previous ``Oana Takakami, Omotesu Otoko-no-Mikoto, and Izanaki-no-Mikoto.'' === History === According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{jalink|Emperor Jinmu|Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{jalink|Amatsukami||Tenjin}} during his {{jalink|Jinmu East Conquest#'Nihonshoki''|Q11590444|Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{jalink|Nihon Shoki|Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{jalink|Uda City|Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. . Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{jalink|Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{jalink|cinnabar|Q104614|tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country. {{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{jalink|Hakuho|Q11580612}}4 years ({{jalink|675 years|Q30523}}) {{jalink|Mizuhanome|Q81 91796|The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{jalink|Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. It is said that in {{jalink|Kanpei|Q1346292}}7 ({{jalink|895|Q31119}}) The mark |Q11444013}} (included in "{{jalink|Ruiju Sandaikaku|Q11665185}}") contains the (Priest)|Q24869239|Celebration}} and {{jalink|Negi|Q11594490}}'s {{jalink|solutions} (Official document)|Q11630902|Answer}}, the book ``Meishin Honki'' says, ``I was founded based on an oracle that said, ``If you enshrine me in a deep mountain where no human voice can be heard, I will rain sweet rain for the world and stop the rain.'''' Original text: ``Nyu Kawakami Amashi Shinto Blessing Negi Doto Interpretation Letter. Inspection of the Gods of God Honkiun. Fumonin's voice of Miyama Yoshino Nyu Kawakami. Tatega Shrine Pillar is worshiped. Tameten descends sweet rain stops the rain. Igami Senzozotensha''. By the way, this {{jalink|official sign}} was created at the time because the nearby {{jalink|peasants|Q843939}} and {{jalink|ronin|Q212418}} often polluted the sacred land. It was issued at the request of the priest of Yamato Shrine, who was in charge of the shrine as a ``Bessatsusha,'' to define the four limits of the shrine's boundaries and impose prohibitions, and the description of the four limits of the shrine played a decisive role in the historical analysis of the Ronsha. . {{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}} ({{jalink|Yamato Shrine|Q245731}}) is said to have been compiled by {{jalink|Kaneki Yoshida|Q723266}}. It is said that it became a annex shrine for the enshrinement of K|Tenri City|Q502196}}, so it is said to have been established by the same Emperor, who had a close relationship with {{jalink|Yoshino|Q15410122}}{{jalink|Hisao Matsuda}}, Research on Niu, Waseda University Press, 1974. . Since ancient times, it has been a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine.According to an old legend, it is said to have been derived from ``Amashi Myojin'' (currently Takanoki Shrine), which is {{jalink|terminal shrine|Q135009906}} of Yamato Shrine. , he was respected by the {{jalink|Imperial Court (Japan)|Q30253177|Imperial Court}} as a ``rain god'' with remarkable miraculous powers for praying for rain, and records show that from 763 to the {{jalink|Onin War|Q385676}}, prayers for rain and offerings to stop the rain were performed 96 times.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://higashiyoshino.com/pg63.html|title=About the history of Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021.119|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Tourism Association}}, {{jalink|Houki|Q18520676}}4 ({{jalink|773|Q31131}}) (Minto)|Q11589711|Kobe}}4 smoke is allocated (``{{jalink|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399}}''). Throughout the {{jalink|ritsuryo system|Q742460}} period, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}}, and together with {{jalink|Kibune Shrine|Q276779|Kifune Shrine}}, it has been entrusted to the {{jalink|Rain Shrine Festival}} to pray for the rain to stop. jalink|hohei|Q11445508}} There are too many examples to enumerate, but on such occasions, the priest of Yamato Shrine was supposed to follow the {{jalink|hohei envoy}} ``Engishiki'' special festival prayer rain god ritual article. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. . In "{{jalink|Engishiki Jinmyocho|Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{jalink|shrine rank #government shrine (shikinaisha)|Q10444029|Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}}3 ({{jalink|1650|Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{jalink|guardian deity|Q97479976}} of {{jalink|Kongōbuji|Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{jalink|Meiji|Q31250 96}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} ({{jalink|Taisho|Q329174}}4), {{jalink|Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{jalink|Modern shrine ranking system|Q712534|Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{jalink|1952|Q5272}} ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}27), and this shrine currently belongs to {{jalink|Shrine Honcho|Q908077}} and is designated as its {{jalink|Bepped Shrine|Q10898274}}. === God level === In {{jalink|Honin|Q1373070}}9 ({{jalink|818|Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{jalink|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{jalink|Jowa (Japan)|Q1075605|Jowa}} 7th year ({{jalink|840|Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{jalink|850 years|Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{jalink|Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{jalink|Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|Jogan}} 1st year ({{jalink|859|Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{jalink|877|Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{jalink|Nihon Sandai Jiroku|Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{jalink|Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{jalink|897|Q30468}}). === Priest === Since the Middle Ages until the {{jalink|Azuchi-Momoyama period|Q319531}}, {{jalink|Ogawa clan|Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{jalink|sub-temple|Q11519671}} served as the {{jalink|Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{jalink|shokan|Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{jalink|Nanbokucho period) (Japan)|Q264012|In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{jalink|Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{jalink|Changroku Incident|Q11653526}}) in {{jalink|Changroku|Q1193524}}2 ({{jalink|1458|Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{jalink|Junkei Tsutsui|Q8192220}} in {{jalink|Tensho|Q1145058}}6 ({{jalink|1578|Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{jalink|1587|Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896. === Precincts === * Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{jalink|Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. :: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall. * Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{jalink|Igyokichi}} in {{jalink|Hirocho|Q1327323}}4 ({{jalink|1264|Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{jalink|Igyosue|Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. * Tea room "Amanu" - {{jalink|1969|Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. * Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{jalink|1940|Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' It is located where the Hiragawa River joins the Takami River, and is said to be the home of the dragon god.As it is located east of the Yoshino Imperial Villa, it has come to be called the "East Falls"{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_15|title=East Waterfall/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. * Setsusha File:Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Sacred tree of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpgFile:Manai (Sacred water) ofNiukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Manai File:Jiji stone and Baba stone of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Torii and Baba stone at the west approach entrance File:Niukawakami-jinja Yumebuchi(Tkami river) 001.jpg|Takami River around Yumebuchi File:Higashi no Taki(East waterfall) of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|East waterfall === Setsusha === === Sessha === * Niu Shrine ** Enshrined deity: Yatsunami no Mikoto :: It is also called the "main shrine" because it is located on the former site of the shrine on the opposite bank of the Mitarai River (Takami River){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_17|title=Setssha/Nyu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}. The main shrine is {{jalink|Kasugazukuri|Q3193781}} thatched roof. :: According to the above-mentioned, {{jalink|Keian|Q1146135}} 3rd year, it was enshrined at that time. By the way, in the {{jalink|1915|Q2084}} (Taisho 4) ``Permission to change the deity enshrined at shrines and change the company name,'' our company ``transferred the Goryodai to the head office and enshrined the appropriate Goryodai at Nyu Shrine.'' File: Higashiyoshino Village Elementary Niu-jinja (Nyu Kawakami Shrine Setsusha) Niu-jinja, Omura 2011.2.22 - panoramio.jpg|Nyu Shrine === Suesha === * Toshogu Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|Tokugawa Ieyasu}}{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_16|title=Summer shrines, Toshogu Shrine and Mizu Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. *Water Shrine - Deities enshrined: Takani no kami (enshrined deity at the upper shrine of Nyukawakami Shrine), Yami no kami (enshrined deity at the lower shrine of Nyu Kawakami Shrine). *Kodama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{jalink|Goju no Mikoto}}. 1982 ({{jalink|Showa|Q327567}}57) To commemorate the 30th anniversary of the opening of the Ogawa-go Timber and Forest Products Cooperative Market, the shrine was founded at the request of {{jalink|Itaigeso Shrine|Q11379271}} (Wakayama City, Wakayama Prefecture){{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_18|title=Suesha/Koda Shrine/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021.11.8|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}. File:Toshogu and Mizu-jinjya of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Toshogu Shrine is on the left of the two shrines on the stone steps, and Mizu Shrine is on the right. File:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 001.jpg|Kodama Shrine Torii and Stone Steps to the ApproachFile:Kodama-jinja of Niukawakami-jinja 002.jpg|Kodama Shrine main building === Annual events === Main festivals {{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=Festivals/Annual Events|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}. *January 16th - Suesha Mizu Shrine Festival *April 16th - Suesha Kirai Shrine Annual Festival *April 17th - Suesha Toshogu Shrine Festival *June 4th - Water God Festival. People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance. *July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival. *Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{jalink|September 16th (lunar calendar)|Q840252|September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato. *October 16th - Annual festival. === Cultural assets === === Important cultural property (designated by the country) === * '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1963|Q2755}} (1963) February 14th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. === Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{jalink|Nyukawa Kaminakasha Shrine Natural Area|Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{jalink|1957|Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{jalink|Evergreen forest|Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{jalink|Aperaceae|Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{jalink|evergreen forests|Q1024867}}. {{jalink|dioecious|Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{jalink|Chii|Q1065400}} and {{jalink|Sakaki|Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons. === Cultural property designated by Nara Prefecture === * '''Wooden Seated Statue of Elephant Goddess, Seated Statue of Male God, Seated Statue of Goddess, Seated Statue of Baby God''' 20 pieces - Designated date: {{jalink|2018|Q25291}} February 2, 2018{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}. One of the statues is a ``Seated Statue of the Elephant Goddess,'' which is 54 centimeters tall and made of {{jalink|one piece of wood}}, and is said to be the oldest statue in Japan dressed in Japanese clothing. In addition, two statues of goddesses in Chinese robes and four statues of male gods were enshrined, both of which are said to have been created in the late {{jalink|History of Japanese Art#Heian Period|Q11508877|Fujiwara Period}}. === Local information === ; Location * {{jalink|Nara Prefecture|Q131287}}{{jalink|Yoshino District|Q1154558}}{{jalink|Higashiyoshino Village|Q1203148}}Oaza and Small 968 ; Transportation access * From {{jalink|Haibara Station|Q5638969}} ({{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1531085|Kintetsu}}{{jalink|Kintetsu Osaka Line|Q1052545|Osaka Line}}, take the {{jalink|Nara Kotsu bus}} bound for Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba and get off at Higashiyoshino Village Yakuba.
